title.en: Lesson 1. The Secret of -(으)세요: The Infix -(으)시-

blocks.md:
Remember back in Stage 4 (`bg-17`) when you learned **-(으)세요**? We noticed that while it is often used as a polite request (*“Please sit down”*), it also appears in statements like *“선생님이 가세요”* (*The teacher is going*).

**Here is the secret you have been waiting for:**

**-(으)세요** is actually made of two distinct parts:
**-(으)시-** *(honorific infix honoring the subject)* + **-어요** *(conversational polite ending)*!

- *가- + -시- + -어요 → 가셔요 → **가세요***
- *앉- + -으시- + -어요 → 앉으셔요 → **앉으세요***

**When do you attach -(으)시-?**

Whenever the **SUBJECT of the sentence** (the person performing the action) is someone you honor or respect:
- Grandparents, parents, teachers, bosses, older relatives, customers, and guests.

**Golden Rule**: You **NEVER** use `-(으)시-` on yourself! (*“제가 가세요”* ❌)

**Connecting to Stage 6 (bg-28)!**

Notice how in the formal register (`-ㅂ/습니다`), `-(으)시-` neatly snaps in: `-(으)시- + -ㅂ니다` → **-(으)십니다** (question: **-(으)십니까?**).

- *“사장님이 지금 회의를 **하십니다**.”* (The CEO is in a meeting right now.)

items.tip: The teacher comes into the classroom.
The CEO is conducting a meeting right now. (Formal)

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly honors the teacher as the subject reading a book?
blocks.why: When the subject is an honored person like a teacher, use -(으)세요: 읽- + -으세요 = 읽으세요. (읽어요 does not honor the teacher, and 읽으십시오 is an imperative command to the listener).

blocks.q: Can you attach -(으)시- to describe your own action? For example: "제가 내일 집에 가세요."
options: No, never honor yourself; say 제가 가요 or 제가 갑니다.
Yes, it makes you sound exceptionally polite to elders.
Yes, but only if you are speaking to younger people.
No, you must replace it with 제가 가십시오.
blocks.why: -(으)시- honors the person performing the action. You never elevate yourself in Korean; always say 제가 가요 or 제가 갑니다.

blocks.q: How do you ask your professor formally: "Are you busy tomorrow?" using 바쁘다?
blocks.why: Formal honorific question: 바쁘- + -시- + -ㅂ니까? = 바쁘십니까? (바쁩니까 lacks the subject honorific -(으)시-, and 바쁘세요 is conversational informal polite).

blocks.meaning: Mother is reading a book in the living room.
blocks.why: 읽다 has batchim, so attach -으세요: 읽- + -으세요 = 읽으세요.

blocks.q: Put in order: "The CEO is holding a meeting right now." (Formal register)

blocks.why: You cannot honor yourself with -(으)시-. Use 가요 or 갑니다: 제가 내일 도서관에 가요.

title.en: Lesson 2. Honorific Particles: 께 and 께서

blocks.md:
In Korean, when you honor someone, you don’t just change the verb ending. **The small particles attached to them upgrade to VIP status as well!**

- **께서**: Replaces **이/가** (subject marker) for honored subjects.
  - *친구**가** 왔어요* → *할머니**께서** 오셨어요*
  - If you want to mark the topic (like **은/는**), you use **께서는**! (*“선생님**께서는** 친절하세요”*)

- **께**: Replaces **에게 / 한테** (*“to / for someone”*) when addressing or giving to an honored recipient.
  - *친구**한테** 줬어요* → *선생님**께** 드렸어요*

head: Role
Everyday Particle
Honorific Particle
Example Sentence
rows: 부모님**께** 편지를 드렸어요. (Wrote letter to parents.)

blocks.md:
**CRITICAL RULE: Harmonic Agreement (짝 맞추기)!**

A very common learner mistake is using `께서` on the subject, but forgetting `-(으)시-` on the verb:

- *할머니께서 집에 와요.* ❌ *(Feels mismatched and incomplete!)*
- *할머니께서 집에 **오세요**.* ⭕

**께서 and -(으)시- move as an inseparable pair!** Whenever you write `께서`, make sure the verb wears its honorific `-(으)시-`!

items.tip: I gave a gift to the teacher. (께 = to teacher)
Father is reading the newspaper. (께서 + 읽으세요)

blocks.q: Which particle correctly replaces 한테/에게 when writing a letter "to my parents"?
blocks.why: The honorific equivalent of 에게/한테 (to an honored recipient) is 께: 부모님께 편지를 썼어요. (께서 is a subject marker).

blocks.q: Which sentence exhibits correct harmonic agreement between subject particle and verb?
blocks.why: 께서 and the honorific verb ending -(으)세요 must match as a pair: 할머니께서 오세요. (할머니께서 와요 has an unhonored verb).

blocks.q: How do you say "The professor is kind" using the honorific topic marker?
blocks.why: The honorific topic marker is 께서는 paired with 친절하세요: 교수님께서는 친절하세요.

blocks.sentence: 내일 스승의 날이라서 선생님[께] 카네이션을 드릴 거예요.
blocks.meaning: Tomorrow is Teacher’s Day, so I will give a carnation to the teacher.
blocks.why: Giving to an honored recipient uses the honorific dative particle 께: 선생님께.

blocks.q: Put in order: "Father is reading a book in the living room."

blocks.why: Harmonic agreement: 께서 pairs with an honorific verb ending: 선생님께서 교실에 오세요.

title.ko: 3강. 종합: -(으)시- · 께서 · 께 한 번에 쓰기
title.en: Lesson 3. Integration: Harmonizing All Honorifics in Real Life

blocks.md:
Now that you know the three pillars of honorific grammar:

1. **-(으)시-**: Verb infix that honors the subject performing the action.
2. **께서**: Upgraded subject particle (*이/가*).
3. **께**: Upgraded recipient particle (*에게/한테*).

Let’s put all three together in real-world scenarios: **at home with family, at school with professors, and at work!**

head: Context
Korean Sentence
Breakdown of Honorifics
English Meaning
rows: Students ask questions to the professor.
The manager explains to the team members.
The guest asks the staff for the menu.

blocks.md:
**Notice Who Gives and Who Receives!**

When **Mother (respected)** calls **Grandmother (even more respected)**:
*“어머니**께서** 할머니**께** 전화를 하세요.”*

- Mother is the subject doing the call → **어머니께서**
- Grandmother is the recipient receiving the call → **할머니께**
- The verb honors mother’s action → **하세요**

Everything snaps together with crystalline clarity!

items.tip: The teacher reads a book for the students. (께서 + -세요)
The department head speaks to us. (Formal workplace)

blocks.q: In the sentence "어머니께서 할머니께 선물을 드렸어요", why is 께 used for 할머니?
options: Because grandmother is the respected recipient receiving the gift
Because grandmother is the subject performing the action
Because mother is giving something to herself
Because 께 is a casual particle for immediate family
blocks.why: 할머니 is the honored recipient receiving the gift, so the honorific dative particle 께 is used.

blocks.q: Which sentence naturally combines 께서 and -(으)세요 in a workplace setting?
blocks.why: 사장님 is honored as the subject with 께서, and the verb takes -세요: 사장님께서 지금 회의실에 들어가세요.

blocks.q: You want to say "The teacher explains to the students." Which sentence is correct?
blocks.why: The teacher is the respected subject (선생님께서), students are ordinary recipients (학생들에게), and the teacher’s action is honored (설명하세요).

blocks.meaning: Mother is making a greeting call to grandmother.
blocks.why: Mother is the respected subject making the phone call: 어머니께서.

blocks.q: Put in order: "Mother is calling grandmother on the phone."
Build the sentence: "Father is reading a book in the living room."
blocks.why: Subject honorific 께서 pairs with 읽으세요: 아버지께서 거실에서 책을 읽으세요.

blocks.hint: Upgrade all three: 어머니가 → 어머니께서, 할머니에게 → 할머니께, 해요 → 하세요.
blocks.why: Honorific agreement: 어머니께서 할머니께 전화를 하세요.

blocks.hint: 께서 requires an honorific verb: 읽다 → 읽으세요
blocks.why: Harmonic agreement: 선생님께서 교실에서 책을 읽으세요.

blocks.q: Mother is calling grandmother.
blocks.why: Both subject (께서) and recipient (께) are honored: 어머니께서 할머니께 전화를 하세요.

blocks.q: The teacher reads a book for the students.
blocks.why: Teacher is honored subject (선생님께서 + 읽어 주세요), students are general recipients (학생들에게).

title.ko: 4강. 실전 대화: 웃어른에 대해 바르게 말하기
title.en: Lesson 4. Speaking Respectfully About Elders in Real Life

blocks.h: Putting Honorifics and Humble Forms into Practice
blocks.md:
In Korean culture, showing respect to elders (parents, grandparents, teachers, bosses) requires **harmonizing the whole sentence**:

1. **The Elder as Subject**: Use **께서** + honorific verb (**-(으)시-** or special words like **주무시다**, **드시다**).
   - 할아버지**께서** 지금 거실에서 **주무세요**.

2. **The Elder as Receiver**: Use **께** + humble verb (**드리다**, **모시다**).
   - 어머니**께** 선물을 **드렸어요**.
   - 할머니를 병원에 **모시고 갔어요**.

3. **Yourself (The Speaker)**: Lower yourself using **저 / 제가** (never 나 / 내가) when speaking to or about elders!

items.tip: Grandmother had her meal deliciously. (Full honorific)
Because it was mother's birthday, I bought and gave her a gift. (Humble 드리다)
I asked the teacher a question. (Humble 여쭤보다)

blocks.q: You are giving flowers to your grandmother on her birthday. How do you say "I gave flowers to grandmother"?
blocks.why: When giving something to an elder, use the particle 께 with the humble verb 드리다: 할머니께 꽃을 드렸어요.

blocks.meaning: Father is sleeping comfortably in the living room.
blocks.why: The honorific equivalent of 자다 (to sleep) for an elder like father is 주무시다: 주무세요.

blocks.q: 모시다 (to take/accompany an elder) — Humble verb: 「주말에 할머니를 병원에 ___ 갔어요.」
blocks.why: When accompanying an elder, use 모시다 instead of 데리다: 모시고 갔어요.

blocks.q: Which sentence shows complete, natural honorific harmony when speaking about a teacher?
options: 선생님께서 학생들에게 책을 읽으면 안 돼요.
blocks.why: 선생님께서 correctly pairs with the honorific past form 읽어 주셨어요.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "Mother calls grandmother every weekend."

blocks.say: 부모님께 안부 전화를 자주 드리는 것이 효도예요.
